ground_truth.unit: change in the probability of believing one does not lose (0/1 outcome)
ground_truth.context: Table 4 ("Effect of Feedback on Belief of Winning"), column (1), the paper's main specification (equation 2), a regression discontinuity in the respondent-specific estimated net gain from the tax and dividend policy.  Among respondents who received the customized win/lose feedback, restricted to those whose estimated net gain is within EUR 50 per year of zero: a linear probability model of the belief after feedback (1 if the respondent believes they do not lose, 0 if they believe they lose) on the predicted-winner indicator (the win feedback, which switches on when the estimated net gain exceeds zero), a quadratic in the estimated net gain, initial acceptance of the tax and dividend, and controls for incomes (piecewise continuous), socio-demographics and other motives.  This is the coefficient on the predicted-winner indicator.

As coded: 0.272 (0.059) (row 6656); no covariates 0.241 (0.056). rdrobust variants (DP58 Table 3, rows 6631-6690): conventional 0.157-0.282, bias-corrected 0.131-0.287; the misclassified respondents dropped (col 6) 0.282 (0.069).

All respondents.

cell.label: claude-code
deviations_manifest: The paper's full control lists are in the online Appendix, which is not available. Controls were constructed as: sociodemographics = sex, age bracket, socio-professional category, education (4 levels), town size, region (factors), household size, number of members aged 14+; incomes = continuous piecewise-linear in income percentiles of respondent and second adult with kinks at p20 and p70 (paper eq. 4); estimated gains = simule_gain and its square; other motives = belief the tax is effective (not 'No') and belief it is progressive (prog_not_no). For Table 8 the other motives are progressivity belief and initial belief of not losing (effectiveness is the endogenous variable).
All regressions use the survey weights (variable weight), since the paper states observations are weighted; heteroskedasticity-robust SEs.

Predicted winner = simule_gagnant (the feedback actually displayed); running variable = simule_gain (estimated net gain per consumption unit); feedback sample = variante_taxe_info == 'f' (1,968). simule_gagnant disagrees with sign(simule_gain) for 56 respondents; used as is.

Yellow Vests supporter = gilets_jaunes_soutien or gilets_jaunes_dedans. Table 4 col 3 controls for the 3-category initial win/lose belief (factor) and interacts the predicted-winner indicator with the binary initial not-lose belief.

Table 6 col 1 subsample: respondent's or second adult's income percentile in [10, 60] (1,969 obs); instruments traite_cible, traite_cible_conjoint and their product; fixed effects for the assigned target (cible); controls single, initial acceptance, incomes, estimated gains, sociodemo, other motives.

Table 8 col 1: info on effectiveness identified as apres_modifs (its label says the second half of the sample received the information on effectiveness against pollution); info on climate change = info_CC.
cell.notes: Independent, blind reproduction from paper text and after_preparation.RData (object s). Exploratory runs attempt-1..6 printed no RESULT lines (attempt-2, 3, 5 crashed because memisc is not installed and memisc item classes had to be stripped; they were exploratory, not repairs). Single scored run (top-level). Caveat: in the Table 8 first stage my effectiveness-information instrument (apres_modifs) is weak (coef ~0.009, joint first-stage F ~2.8), suggesting the variable or control set may differ from the authors'; I did not change the specification after seeing this, per blind-mode rules. While exploring the RData (attempt-1) the listing printed the bodies of some utility functions stored in the RData (plotting/formatting helpers, weighting_s, piece.formula); none of the paper's analysis code was read. No docker hang.
